sections.title: Stopping times, optional sampling and integrability conditions

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-optional-stopping-and-random-walks-C009 (partial): Hypotheses not supplied: an unstated assumption. The statement of Wald's second identity (handbook/parts/p15/optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex lines 174-179) asserts that S_{T and n} -> S_T in L2 and ES_T^2 = sigma^2 ET for any T with ET<infinity. It never says T is a stopping time. Every other sampling entry in the chapter does declare it, at lines 48, 65, 79, 97, 119, 162 and 195. The held source's Exercise 4.8.4 (Durrett v5, printed p. 261 = PDF p. 269) states 'if T is a stopping time with ET<infinity'. The annex proof relies on the property without stating it: annex line 186 uses that {T>=j} is F_{j-1}-measurable. The source hypothesis is therefore not preserved. The omission matters: with fair signs, let T=1 on {xi_1=xi_2} and T=2 otherwise. Then ES_T^2 = 1/2, but sigma^2 ET = 3/2. The exit-time bound, its strict form and the sigma^2=0 case are present.

ED26-P15-CH-optional-stopping-and-random-walks-C020 (partial): The construction or argument is not fully written. To prove E_x tau<infinity, the annex chooses delta>0 with P(xi_1>=delta)>0 (handbook/annex/p15/optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex line 597). That requires ruling out xi_1<=0 a.s. The text argues only the case xi_1>=0 a.s., which the proof never uses. The case it does use is dismissed as 'the nonpositive case is analogous' (line 595), which counts as a 'similarly' step in an owed proof. Three results depend on this finiteness: the overshoot integrability E_x e^{theta S_tau} <= e^{theta a} E_x tau (line 628), the exact identity E_x e^{theta_0 S_tau} = e^{theta_0 x} (lines 629-630) and the lower-exit bound. The one-sided bound for the possibly infinite T (lines 635-646) does not depend on it.
